sentences.text: Arackar is an extinct genus of lithostrotian sauropod that may belong to the family Saltasauridae.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes neck and back vertebrae, a humerus, a femur, and an ischium, representing a juvenile individual.
A distinctive feature of this animal is a high and wide hollow between the prearticular process and the vertebral body.
This young individual had an estimated body length of around 6.3 meters.
The species name licanantay translates to 'bones of the Atacamans' in the Kunza language.
The holotype is the most complete sauropod specimen known from Chile.
The size of a fully grown Arackar is currently unknown.

The holotype specimen was discovered in 1993 at Quebrada La Higuera, about 75 km south of Copiapó, and the species Arackar licanantay was named and described in 2021 by a team led by David Rubilar-Rogers.
Expeditions in 2006, 2007, and 2011 found an additional specimen preserved in similar conditions about 100 meters from the holotype.
Arackar is classified within Titanosauria and Lithostrotia as a sister taxon to Isisaurus.
Arackar forms a clade with Rapetosaurus and is possibly part of the Saltasauridae family.

Arackar lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 83.3 and 66 million years ago, in what is now South America. The time range for Arackar spans from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
